name: BTCPay Server
purpose: Self-hosted, open-source Bitcoin payment processor: stores, invoices, point of sale, payment requests and pull payments, paid on chain or over Lightning straight into the merchant's own wallet, with the Greenfield REST API for integrations.

maintenance.evidence: v2.4.5 published on 2026-10-06; repository pushed on 2026-10-23 and not archived.

platforms.other: Linux through btcpayserver-docker (btcpay-setup.sh installs Docker and Docker Compose when needed), one-click hosting such as LunaNode, cloud and VPS providers (not OpenVZ) and hardware builds. Manual installation and building without Docker are rated very hard and for development; the deployment guide does not mention Windows.

interfaces.description: Greenfield API v1 under /api/v1: GET /api/v1/health without authentication ({synchronized}); GET /api/v1/server/info with any key (version, onion, supportedPaymentMethods, fullySynched, syncStatus[] with paymentMethodId, chainHeight, syncHeight, available); GET /api/v1/stores and /api/v1/stores/{storeId} (btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/invoices with take, skip, status, startDate and endDate (btcpay.store.canviewinvoices; status is New, Processing, Settled, Expired or Invalid, amounts are decimal strings, times Unix seconds); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/payment-methods (btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings; ids such as BTC-CHAIN, BTC-LN and BTC-LNURL); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/payment-methods/{paymentMethodId}/wallet (btcpay.store.canviewwallet: balance, confirmedBalance, unconfirmedBalance); GET /api/v1/stores/{storeId}/lightning/{cryptoCode}/info (btcpay.store.canuselightningnode).
interfaces.authentication: API key sent as Authorization: token {key}, or HTTP Basic where the user allows it. Keys carry chosen permissions, never more than the user's own, optionally limited to one store (permission:storeId); /api-keys/authorize opens a form in BTCPay that creates a key with the permissions named in the link.

interfaces.description: Store webhooks: invoice and payout events posted to a URL the merchant sets, signed in the BTCPay-Sig header as sha256=HMAC256(secret, body).
interfaces.authentication: HMAC signature with the webhook's secret.

interfaces.description: Web interface for stores, invoices, wallets, apps and server administration, served by the deployment's reverse proxy.

cli: The Docker deployment installs command-line utilities with btcpay-setup.sh -i; btcpay-backup.sh (as root, stops the stack while archiving; BTCPAY_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE encrypts the archive) and btcpay-restore.sh restore a deployment.
remoteManagement: The Greenfield API over HTTPS with API keys and the web interface; the Docker deployment itself is administered on its host, usually over SSH, with its scripts.
nodeCompatibility: Uses NBXplorer as its chain indexer over a Bitcoin full node (Bitcoin Core in the Docker deployment); syncStatus reports each chain's indexer height. Lightning through a node the store connects to (the Docker deployment offers LND, Core Lightning or Eclair).

dependencies.notes: Its chain indexer; part of every deployment.
For Lightning payments; the Docker deployment can also run Eclair.
The server can be reached through an onion service, which server info reports.

networking: The Docker deployment serves the web interface and API behind its reverse proxy on ports 80 and 443, which must be reachable from the internet for its automatic HTTPS certificate; webhooks go out to the merchant's URLs.
storage: Docker volumes for BTCPay, NBXplorer, the node and the databases (PostgreSQL is part of the standard stack); the install example uses the opt-save-storage-xs fragment for a pruned node. Sizes not measured here.
security: An API key acts with the permissions it was given, limited by its user's rights, so a read-only monitor needs only btcpay.store.canviewstoresettings, btcpay.store.canviewinvoices and, for balances, btcpay.store.canviewwallet; btcpay.store.canuselightningnode lets a key use the store's Lightning node, including paying with it. Backups made by btcpay-backup.sh contain secrets and, with Lightning, the wallet and channel.backup: old channel state is dangerous and restoring the archive alone does not recover channels.
integrationMechanisms: Call the Greenfield API with an API key the user creates with read-only permissions
Open /api-keys/authorize with exactly those permissions so the key is created in BTCPay itself
Watch /api/v1/health and server info for availability and synchronisation

feasibility.notes: Connecting to an existing installation is straightforward and needs no software on Windows; deploying one needs Docker on Linux or a hosting provider, which BTCortex does not set up.

notes: Other entries of the payments, sidechains and mining scope are still to be researched.

sources.title: Back up and restore the Docker deployment

unverifiedClaims: Running btcpayserver-docker under WSL2 or Docker Desktop on Windows is not documented and was not tried.
Disk and memory needs of a deployment were not measured.

name: Nutshell (Cashu)
purpose: Chaumian ecash wallet and mint for Bitcoin Lightning based on the Cashu protocol: the reference Python implementation, with a command-line wallet and a mint backed by a Lightning node.

platforms.windowsDistribution: Python package (pip install cashu); the README gives Windows commands for a Python 3.12 virtual environment
platforms.other: Python 3.10 or later on PyPI (the README recommends 3.12, since 3.13 and 3.14 fail to build coincurve); Docker image cashubtc/nutshell:0.21.0.

interfaces.description: The mint’s Cashu API; the Docker example listens on port 3338 (MINT_LISTEN_PORT).

nodeCompatibility: The mint needs a Lightning back end chosen with MINT_BACKEND_BOLT11_SAT, such as LND or Core Lightning; FakeWallet serves tests without one.

dependencies.notes: For a mint (FakeWallet only for tests).

networking: The mint serves HTTP (port 3338 in the Docker example).
security: A mint holds the bitcoin behind its tokens, so its users trust it with their funds; running one means holding other people’s money. The public test mint is for demonstration only and its satoshis are not real.

feasibility.notes: Running a mint makes the user custodian of other people’s funds, which is outside what BTCortex sets up.

unverifiedClaims: Running the mint or wallet on Windows was not tried.

name: CDK mint (cdk-mintd)
purpose: Cashu mint from the Cashu Development Kit, a collection of Rust crates for Cashu wallets and mints, with Lightning back ends for LND, Core Lightning and LDK Node.
nodeCompatibility: Lightning back ends cdk-lnd, cdk-cln and cdk-ldk-node; cdk-fake-wallet fills quotes automatically for tests; LNbits only through an external payment processor (cdk-payment-processor).

dependencies.notes: A Lightning back end for the mint.

security: Its README says the project is in early development but works with real sats, so only amounts one does not mind losing should be used; a mint holds its users’ funds.

feasibility.notes: Early-stage custodial software for its users.

unverifiedClaims: Windows support, ports and container images were not checked.

name: Fedimint
purpose: Module-based system for building federated applications, shipping Bitcoin, Lightning and Chaumian ecash modules: a federation of servers (fedimintd) holds funds together and issues ecash, with Lightning gateways (gatewayd).

maintenance.evidence: v0.12.2 and v0.11.4 published on 2026-10-06; v0.13.0-beta.1 (a pre-release) on 2026-10-09.

platforms.other: Linux x86_64 binaries, .deb and .rpm packages (fedimintd, gatewayd, fedimint-cli, gateway-cli, fedimint-dbtool, fedimint-recoverytool, devimint) and macOS aarch64 archives.

cli: fedimintd (guardian server), gatewayd (Lightning gateway), fedimint-cli, gateway-cli, fedimint-dbtool, fedimint-recoverytool.
nodeCompatibility: The Bitcoin module follows the chain (how guardians connect to a node was not examined); gateways connect the federation to Lightning.
security: The federation’s servers hold the funds together (the README links to its dealer-free distributed key generation); users trust the federation, not a single mint.

feasibility.notes: No Windows builds, and running a guardian means holding funds with others.

notes: Client applications listed in the README include Fedi, Ecash App, Conduit Wallet, Harbor Wallet and Vipr Wallet.
unverifiedClaims: How guardians connect to their Bitcoin node, and the ports used, were not examined.

name: Elements
purpose: Open-source, sidechain-capable blockchain platform derived from Bitcoin; elementsd -chain=liquidv1 runs a node of the Liquid Network.

maintenance.evidence: elements-23.3.4 published on 2026-09-09; release candidates elements-23.4.0rc3 (2026-07-06) and elements-29.4.1rc1 (2026-08-12) are in testing.

platforms.windowsDistribution: elements-23.3.4-win64.zip and elements-23.3.4-win64-setup-unsigned.exe, with SHA256SUMS and its signatures (SHA256SUMS.asc)
platforms.other: Linux (x86_64, aarch64, arm, powerpc64, riscv64) and macOS archives.

interfaces.description: Bitcoin Core-style JSON-RPC with Elements’ additions (assets, peg-ins).

nodeCompatibility: A Liquid node validates peg-ins against a Bitcoin node (not examined here). PeerSwap’s L-BTC swaps need an Elements back end that follows the post-ELIP 203 chain tip.
security: The Windows installer of 23.3.4 is published as unsigned; the archives are covered by SHA256SUMS and its signatures.

feasibility.notes: Windows archives with signed checksums make a managed Liquid node possible, but BTCortex has no Liquid features that would use it.

unverifiedClaims: Who signs SHA256SUMS.asc was not identified.
Peg-in validation settings, disk and memory needs of a Liquid node were not examined.
What ELIP 203 changed (mentioned in PeerSwap’s README) was not examined.

name: SideSwap
purpose: Cross-platform, non-custodial wallet and atomic-swap marketplace for the Liquid Network: trades between Liquid assets (L-BTC, USDt, EURx, AMP tokens) and peg-in and peg-out bridging.

platforms.other: Android (APKs, also for F-Droid), Linux AppImage, macOS, iOS.

nodeCompatibility: Liquid wallet; it does not use the user’s Bitcoin node (not examined further).
security: Users keep their keys; Liquid’s Confidential Transactions hide amounts and asset types on chain.
integrationMechanisms: Launch the user’s own installation (not built)

feasibility.notes: A native Windows application, but outside BTCortex’s Bitcoin-node features.

unverifiedClaims: The architecture of the Windows installer and its signing were not checked.

name: AQUA
purpose: Free, open-source wallet for iOS and Android, from JAN3.

maintenance.evidence: v0.5.4 published on 2026-10-01 (an Android APK, aqua-0.5.4-273.apk).

feasibility.notes: A phone wallet with nothing for BTCortex to connect to.

unverifiedClaims: Which networks it supports and whether it can use the user’s own node were not checked; its README says only that it is a free, open-source wallet for iOS and Android.

name: Alby JS SDK
purpose: JavaScript SDK for Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47) and the Alby API.

interfaces.authentication: A nostr+walletconnect:// connection string with its secret.

nodeCompatibility: Talks to any NWC wallet service, such as Alby Hub.
security: An NWC connection string carries a secret that lets its holder use the wallet within the permissions granted.

feasibility.notes: A library for wallet applications; BTCortex does not offer NWC.

notes: Alby Hub, the main NWC wallet service, is recorded as alby-hub; the protocol is recorded as nip-47.

name: Stratum V2 Reference Implementation (SRI)
purpose: Reference implementation of the Stratum V2 mining protocol: protocol crates (stratum) and applications (sv2-apps) — a pool server, the job declarator server and client that let miners build their own block templates, and a translator proxy for SV1 miners.

maintenance.evidence: sv2-apps v0.8.0 and the stratum crates v1.12.0 published on 2026-09-17.

platforms.other: miner-apps and pool-apps archives for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, musl) and macOS (x86_64 and aarch64).

interfaces.description: Stratum V2 (and SV1 through the translator proxy) towards miners and pools; Template Distribution from Bitcoin Core’s IPC interface.

cli: pool, jd-server, jd-client and translator applications.
nodeCompatibility: Its bitcoin-core-sv2 crate translates Bitcoin Core’s IPC interface into Stratum V2 Template Distribution; Bitcoin Core’s Windows builds have no IPC interface (no bitcoin-node.exe; see bitcoin-core).

dependencies.notes: Built with the IPC interface, which Windows builds lack.

security: Application crates in alpha, according to both READMEs.

feasibility.notes: Alpha software that needs Bitcoin Core’s IPC interface, which Bitcoin Core does not build for Windows.

unverifiedClaims: Ports and configuration of the applications were not examined.

name: DATUM Gateway
purpose: Mining gateway that lets miners mine with block templates made by their own Bitcoin node, speaking Stratum v1 to mining hardware; used with the OCEAN pool.

maintenance.evidence: v0.5.1beta and v0.5.0beta published on 2026-10-19; the README says the gateway remains in public beta.

platforms.other: OCEAN’s Debian packages for Debian Trixie on amd64 (with Bitcoin Core), Debian’s own package, a DATUM box installer image, source builds and Docker, according to the README.

interfaces.description: Stratum v1 towards mining hardware; RPC with getblocktemplate towards the node.

nodeCompatibility: Needs a valid Bitcoin node with RPC and getblocktemplate; Bitcoin Core is the recommended node. Its README says Bitcoin Knots versions after 29.3.knots20260507 are no longer compatible and would earn no mining rewards.

dependencies.notes: RPC with getblocktemplate; the recommended node.
Knots after 29.3.knots20260507 (the releases that follow another chain) are no longer compatible.

security: Public beta. The README warns to check which network a fork mines, and how work is rewarded, before pointing hashpower at it.
licenceNotes: Copyright Bitcoin Ocean, LLC, Jason Hughes and contributors.

feasibility.notes: No Windows build; mining set-ups are outside BTCortex’s scope today.

unverifiedClaims: Its Stratum port, node settings (blocknotify) and build dependencies are in INSTALL.md, which was not read.

name: Public Pool
purpose: Bitcoin Stratum mining server written in TypeScript with NestJS, run against the user’s own node.

maintenance.evidence: No releases are published; the releases feed was updated on 2026-10-23.

platforms.other: Built and run with Docker or Docker Compose from the repository (Compose binds the Stratum ports to 127.0.0.1).

nodeCompatibility: Connects to the node’s RPC; with Docker, the README adds rpcallowip=172.16.0.0/12 to bitcoin.conf.
security: Opening the node’s RPC to Docker’s network range lets containers reach it.
licenceNotes: No licence is stated in the README and no LICENSE file was found.

feasibility.notes: Docker-only set-up and no stated licence.

unverifiedClaims: Whether it is meant for solo mining is not stated in the README.

name: ckpool
purpose: Low-overhead, massively scalable mining pool server in C for Linux, which also works as a proxy, passthrough, node, redirector or solo pool (BTCSOLO mode).

maintenance.evidence: The Bitbucket repository was updated on 2026-10-14; it publishes no releases.

nodeCompatibility: At least one bitcoind with server, rpcuser and rpcpassword set; ZMQ block notifications need the node’s -zmqpubhashblock.
security: Its README asks operators to keep the default 0.5% development contribution on blocks found in pool mode.

name: Braiins OS
purpose: Custom firmware for Bitcoin ASICs (Bitmain Antminer models) with autotuning, Stratum V2 support and gRPC APIs; Braiins Toolbox manages many miners from a desktop application.

maintenance.evidence: The product page lists current models such as the S21 series and T21.

platforms.other: Firmware for Antminer S21, S21 Pro, S21+, T21, S19 series, S17 and S9 variants.

remoteManagement: Its gRPC APIs and Braiins Toolbox.
nodeCompatibility: Mines for a pool; Stratum V2, with a V2-to-V1 translation proxy for pools that only speak V1.
security: It directs a 2–2.5% development fee of the hashrate (depending on the model) to Braiins’ pool.
licenceNotes: A licence agreement that allows use with the development fee (braiins.com/os/plus/license); not open source as far as the page states.

feasibility.notes: ASIC firmware, outside what BTCortex manages.

unverifiedClaims: Its version history, whether Braiins Toolbox runs on Windows, and its API documentation were not examined.

name: ESP-Miner (AxeOS)
purpose: Open-source ESP32 firmware for the Bitaxe open-hardware miner, with the AxeOS web interface and a REST API on the device.

platforms.other: Firmware for Bitaxe boards with the ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 N16R8 module (factory images per board version, and esp-miner.bin); flashed with bitaxetool.

interfaces.description: AxeOS web interface at the device’s address on the local network (http://bitaxe with mDNS) and its REST API, for example GET /api/system/info and PATCH /api/system.

cli: bitaxetool flashes the firmware and its configuration.
remoteManagement: The device’s REST API on the local network.
nodeCompatibility: Mines for the Stratum pool configured on the device, such as a pool run on the user’s node.
security: The README’s API examples use no authentication, so anyone on the local network may be able to read and change the device’s settings.
integrationMechanisms: Read hashrate, temperature and pool state from /api/system/info for monitoring (not built)

feasibility.notes: A read-only REST API on the local network would let BTCortex show a home miner, but mining is outside its features today.

unverifiedClaims: Whether the API can require authentication was not checked.

name: cgminer
purpose: Long-standing ASIC and FPGA miner software in C.

maintenance.evidence: The latest tag is v4.11.1 from 2018-08-16.

unverifiedClaims: Its API and Windows support were not examined.
